outcome: hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn
proportion of RhD-negative pregnancies and newborns
maternal spontaneous anti-D antibody sensitization rate
cohort: The study participants were 1062 RhD-negative pregnant women who delivered at 22 weeks or later at 47 Japanese facilities between April 2018 and March 2023.
finding: Sensitized RhD-negative women experienced higher rates of adverse perinatal outcomes including cesarean section, preterm delivery, neonatal hemolytic anemia, and NICU admissions compared to non-sensitized women.
mod_finding: Sensitized RhD-negative women had higher rates of cesarean section.
